question.text: Which of the following is TRUE about put-option embedded bonds (putable bonds)?

answer.text: They yield higher than comparable plain vanilla bonds
They yield lower than comparable plain vanilla bonds (bondholder pays for the option)

explanation.text: The Logic: Putable = bondholder has right to sell back = embedded option value. Bondholders pay (lower yield) for this protection. The Trap: Callable bonds (issuer option) yield MORE than plain vanilla because the bondholder is 'short' the call. Putable is the opposite. Cross-Exam Context: IV Ch 4 covers embedded options; XXI-B tests. Manager's Pro-Tip: Putable bonds are rare in Indian market; callable PSU bonds are more common. Model call-option cost into yield calculations.
